page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 2400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance profiles. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, with read-only speeds reaching 189.99 GB/sec and write speeds at 91.19 GB/sec. Passmark database operations are also strong at 21,664.66. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU, gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, remains in the average tier. Large language model inference tasks show weak to poor performance, particularly for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5d.16xlarge offers high resource density by combining a substantial vCPU count with bundled high-speed local NVMe storage. This configuration reduces the need for external block storage attachments for high-throughput local operations. The hardware profile is suited for workloads such as database operations, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and software compilation, where the combination of dedicated compute cores, large memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage can be fully leveraged.
